coreHolding: 101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024). Invalidated VA's single-step ceiling on 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4), holding veterans at base rates SMC(l)–(n) are entitled to multiple half-step or full-step intermediate SMC increases (capped at SMC(o)) for each separate 50% or 100% disability. (Caution: Attacking final pre-May 2024 single-step ratings via CUE faces 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) / George v. McDonough change-in-interpretation defenses).
veteranPlainSummary: Federal Circuit ruling holding that severely disabled Veterans receiving Special Monthly Compensation (SMC l–n) can earn multiple half-step or full-step increases up to SMC(o) for each additional 50% or 100% disability (applies to open/pending claims; final pre-May 2024 ratings face § 20.1403(e) CUE limits).

coreHolding: (1) Obesity per se is not a "disease or injury" under 38 U.S.C. §§ 1110, 1131 and cannot be rated as a standalone SC disability; HOWEVER, (2) obesity may serve as an "intermediate step" establishing secondary service connection under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310 when an SC orthopedic/mental/endocrine condition causes weight gain (or prevents exercise) that proximately causes or aggravates a third disability (e.g., obstructive sleep apnea, hypertension, diabetes, GERD, or contralateral joint disease)!
litigationUtility: Cornerstone Secondary SC Play: Develop three explicit nexus links in the private IMO/DBQ: (a) SC condition caused/aggravated obesity (immobility, SSRIs/corticosteroids, PTSD binge eating); (b) obesity was a substantial factor causing/aggravating the downstream condition; and (c) the downstream condition would not have occurred (or worsened) to the same degree absent the SC disability.
